Sam (Product): ok team, Q2 planning sync — need to lock a single launch slice for the hosted inference surface. customers are pushing on embeddings cold-start latency and chat streaming at scale. want to propose 3 candidate bets and get quick thumbs: 1) Embedding warmup + cache priming flow, 2) Rerank throughput improvements, 3) Chat streaming stability + fallback. which should we prioritize for the release window?

Maya (Eng): +1 to picking one focused bet. our biggest op cost right now is tail latency from model cold starts for embeddings. warmup could be low-risk and high-impact.

Ken (ML): embedding warmup helps, but depending on quantization mode we still see 20-30% quality variance. if we do an automated priming prompt pipeline we should include a quality check step.

Priya (Design): from a UX POV, customers want consistent first-token latency for embeddings (search relevance pipelines break otherwise). we can add a progress indicator in the console while priming runs.

Sam (Product): draft launch criteria (proposal):
- Embeddings: median first-token latency <= 120ms for small inputs, p95 <= 400ms; automated priming pipeline that runs on first deploy + after model swap; metrics surfaced in Console.
- Rerank: 2x throughput vs current baseline for typical 8-doc rerank with batch size 16; fallback to lower-cost model when overloaded.
- Chat streaming: <150ms per token at steady state; graceful fallback to non-streaming when network issues.
Can we map feasibility to those?

Maya (Eng): feasible but notes: "median first-token <=120ms" requires warm pool of <4s idle TTL and a priming strategy that doesn't burn tokens. we can use a truncated prompt for priming ("warm-token" pattern) + internal cache. risk: extra token costs and KPS on the serving cluster.

Ken (ML): quality check idea: after priming, run 10 seeding prompts and compute embedding drift vs baseline. regression threshold = cosine < 0.985. if regression, auto-fallback to non-primed variant + alert.

Zach (SRE): from infra side we need an ops guardrail: priming jobs need to be rate-limited by account and zone. also add a canary rollout: 5% customers (low-traffic tenants) -> 25% -> 100% with health checks. deploy-bot: please add canary stages to the release pipeline.

deploy-bot: created release plan: canary=5% for 24h -> 25% for 48h -> global. health checks: p95 latency, error rate, CPU/GPU duty cycle.

Priya (Design): acceptance criteria for console: "Priming status" appears in model details; priming logs link to per-tenant metrics. customers can opt-out.

Sam (Product): ok owners:
- Spec + product signoff: Sam
- Priming implementation + throttle: Maya
- Embedding drift checks + thresholds: Ken
- Console surface + opt-out: Priya
- Canary + rollout automation: Zach

Maya (Eng): implementation note: suggest adding a cheap LRU priming cache keyed by (model-version, tenant-id, input-shape-bucket). reduces repeated priming for multi-tenant calls.

Ken (ML): agree. also recommend an offline eval harness: run the priming strategy against our 3 benchmark corpora and measure recall/precision impact on downstream retrieval. want to catch any regressions before canary.

Priya (Design): small copy for console: "Model priming reduces first-request latency by warming internal caches. Priming may consume a small number of tokens. You can opt out in Settings."

Sam (Product): risks we should call out publicly in the PRD: token cost, potential regression on quantized models, extra complexity in rollout, per-tenant rate limits. mitigation: drift check + auto-fallback + opt-out.

Zach (SRE): can we define rollout health signals? propose:
- latency_p95_increase < +10% vs baseline
- error_rate < 0.1%
- GPU_duty_cycle < 85%
if any breach -> auto-rollback to previous model variant.

Maya (Eng): agree, but add "priming queue length" alert to catch priming buildup during traffic spikes.

Sam (Product): decision for this thread: move forward with bet #1 (Embeddings warmup + priming + console surface) as the Q2 hosted-inference slice. do we have thumbs?

Ken (ML): :thumbsup:

Maya (Eng): :thumbsup: I'll start a PRD draft and link infra constraints.

Priya (Design): :thumbsup: will drop console mocks into the PRD.

Zach (SRE): :thumbsup: will add canary steps to pipeline.

Sam (Product): thanks — action items summarised: Sam write final PRD by EOD Friday; Maya to prototype priming LRU + TTL; Ken to run offline eval for drift; Priya to produce mocks; Zach to update canary plan. follow-up sync next Tue 10am.

Maya (Eng): quick Q — what token budget should priming assume per tenant? propose 50 tokens per model-version warmup, with burst allowance for high-throughput tenants.

Ken (ML): 50 seems reasonable for truncated prompt; we'll validate in eval.

Sam (Product): ok set 50 tokens default. can change after eval.

Zach (SRE): added note: billing should be explicit — priming tokens billed to tenant usage but flagged in billing export.

Sam (Product): good call. last note: can someone add a short snippet for ops runbook on how to force-clear priming cache for a tenant? we should document it.

Maya (Eng): I'll add ops command in the PRD: `redwood priming clear --tenant <id> --model <version>`

Sam (Product): perfect. thanks everyone.
